tagline: Marshes, prairie and Gulf beaches share a network of coastal highways.
intro: The Creole Nature Trail connects marshland, prairie and sandy beaches across a 180-mile network of highways in southwestern Louisiana. It follows mainly LA 27 and LA 82 in Cameron and Calcasieu parishes, with four wildlife refuges along the route. The Federal Highway Administration’s archived All-American Road account highlights wildflowers, alligators, birds and cheniers shaped by salty winds. That account allows four or five hours of driving, depending on the route, or two days to visit.

The trail gathers existing state highways into a byway rather than following one purpose-built road. Holly Beach began appearing on official highway maps in 1948. Hurricane Audrey devastated the community in 1957, after which several houses were raised. Rita devastated it again in 2005.

For a southbound approach, LA 27 connects Sulphur through Carlyss with Holly Beach on the Gulf. Sabine National Wildlife Refuge lies along that highway between Hackberry and Holly Beach. At Holly Beach, turn east toward Cameron, ten miles away; the highways cross the Calcasieu Ship Channel just west of town. LA 27 and LA 82 pass through Cameron as Marshall Street. This section brings the marshes between Sabine and Calcasieu lakes into the same journey as Holly Beach’s Gulf shore and Cameron’s river mouth.

moments.title: Sabine National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Sabine’s marsh refuge stretches between Sabine Lake on the west and Calcasieu Lake at its eastern tip. More than 200 bird species live here, including great egrets, Neotropic cormorants and shorebirds. The Wetland Walkway is a 1.5-mile concrete nature trail with a wooden-boardwalk section, an observation tower and fifteen interpretive stations on Gulf Coast marshland. Hurricane Rita hit the refuge directly in 2005; its office buildings, visitor center and maintenance shops were damaged beyond repair and removed. American alligators, blue crabs, mink, river otters and turtles are also among the refuge’s wildlife.

moments.title: Holly Beach
moments.text: Holly Beach, a coastal community in Cameron Parish, is also known as the Cajun Riviera. Its beachfront cabins were known as camps, and the community began appearing on official highway maps in 1948. In 1957, Hurricane Audrey brought a twelve-foot storm surge; afterward, several houses were altered to stand taller. Rita devastated the town in 2005, and Gustav and Ike flooded it again in 2008. The place also has a musical history: Nathan Abshire recorded a Holly Beach waltz, and Kenny Tibbs and the Jokers made it the subject of a swamp-pop song in 1991.

moments.title: Cameron
moments.text: Cameron’s position at the mouth of the Calcasieu River made it a transfer point for mail, cattle and other goods bound by ship for Lake Charles. Originally named Leesburg, Cameron became a petroleum-extraction center after Louisiana’s first successful oil well in 1901. Hurricanes repeatedly damaged the parish seat. After Rita and Ike destroyed successive libraries, the main parish library was rebuilt on tall stilts. Laura destroyed or severely damaged much of the town again in 2020. LA 27 and LA 82 share Marshall Street through the community, crossing the ship channel just west of town.
